question: Question linked to image nº9 A 35-year-old woman comes to the consultation because she presents chest pain when she is struggling. It does not have cardiovascular risk factors. A systolic murmur is heard in aortic focus that increases with the Valsalva maneuver. The ECG shows sinus rhythm, Q waves, repolarization disorders and left ventricular hypertrophy criteria. In the figure you can see an image of your echocardiography. Point to the FALSE option:

options.opb: This disease is associated with sudden death.
options.opc: Atrial fibrillation has a higher incidence in people with this disease.
options.opd: Dyspnea will not appear until the patient develops left ventricular systolic dysfunction.

paths: (Hypertrophy, Left Ventricular)-CAUSES->(Hypertensive disease)-CAUSES->(Left ventricular systolic dysfunction)
(Hypertrophy, Left Ventricular)-PREDISPOSES->(Myocardial Infarction)-CAUSES->(Left ventricular systolic dysfunction)

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Aortic stenosis -> left ventricular hypertrophy -> increased risk of sudden death -> 80% CHAIN: Aortic stenosis -> left ventricular hypertrophy -> dyspnea can occur before left ventricular systolic dysfunction -> 75% CHAIN: Aortic stenosis -> left ventricular hypertrophy -> increased risk of atrial fibrillation -> 70% CHAIN: Aortic stenosis -> left ventricular hypertrophy -> not always a hereditary disease -> 80%
enhanced_information: The FALSE option is opc. Atrial fibrillation has a higher incidence in people with this disease. While aortic stenosis and left ventricular hypertrophy can predispose to atrial fibrillation, the statement that atrial fibrillation has a higher incidence in people with this disease is false based on standard consensus. The evidence paths support the relationship between left ventricular hypertrophy and atrial fibrillation but do not specifically address the incidence in this disease.
analysis: The core medical principle here is that atrial fibrillation is not specifically linked to a higher incidence in this disease, although it can be associated with left ventricular hypertrophy. Aortic stenosis with left ventricular hypertrophy can predispose to atrial fibrillation, but the statement that atrial fibrillation has a higher incidence in people with this disease is not directly supported by consensus. The focus should be on the relationship between aortic stenosis, left ventricular hypertrophy, and the associated symptoms.
